corrections.reason: Stage 1 produced a non-Ethiopic Thai character 'เ' and 'ገ' for the two-legged Fidel 'ዝ' in 'ዝማም ወርቅ' (pure/refined gold), which also recurs in L12.
The printed glyph has two vertical legs with the top-right bar of 'ዝ' ('ዝማም ወርቅ'), misread as single-legged 'ገ'.
The standard Amharic conjunction 'ነገር ግን' is printed with 1st-order 'ገ', misread as 6th-order 'ግ'.
In Classical Ge'ez (Luke 16:18), 'another (fem. acc.)' is 'ካልእተ' with 'እ', clearly visible on the page.

Looking at the image, the Ge'ez text is 'ወእንተኒ ይኀድጋ ምታ' (or 'ይኀድግ ምታ' / 'ይሞት ምታ'—actually inspecting the glyphs closely: 'ይኀድጋ' or 'ይኅድጋ' or 'ይነሥእ'? Let's check the image: it has 3 letters: ይ - ኅ/ኀ - ድ/ሬ? No, the Amharic translation in L07 says 'ባሏ የሞተባትም' (and she whose husband died), which in Ge'ez is 'ወእንተኒ ይመውት ምታ' or 'ይኅልፍ ምታ'! Wait: looking at the 3 glyphs in L05: ይ - ኃ/ኅ - ሬ/ልፍ? No, it is 3 letters: ይ - ኃ - ሬ. Keep as printed or check carefully).
Joining L26-27 gives 'ነበረ ።' (there was), printed with 1st-order 'ረ', not 6th-order 'ር'.
The printed text reads 'እንደሆነ የተመቸ ከታወቀ' (just as in L30 'እንደሆነ'), with 1st-order 'ደ' and 'ቸ'.

Wait: looking at L33 in Col 2 and comparing with Col 3 L12-13 ('ፈጽሞ ደግ የለምና ጥቂት ጽነት ነበረችውና'), in Col 2 L33 it is the contrast: for a sinner except the devil, there is no one completely evil/hardened ('ጽኑዕ' / 'ጽኑነ' / 'ጽነት'). Looking at the glyph in Col 2 L33: ጽ-ኑ-ዕ or ጽ-ና-ት? It has ጽ - ኑ - ዕ (3 letters: ጽኑዕ).
The demonstrative genitive is 'የዚያን ዋጋ' (the reward of that, parallel to Col 3 L13 'የዚያን ፍዳ'), where 'ያ' with a faded top loop was misread as 'ሀ'.
